newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasani says won't overpay for Interleisure.
newsitem.headline: Sasani says won't overpay for Interleisure.

text.p: South Africa's Sasani Ltd said on Tuesday it will not overpay to secure a stake in cinema to film production firm Interleisure Ltd and questioned whether the firm could be bought at a "realistic" price.

"There is a price at which Sasani will not go beyond in terms of this deal...The worst scenario for Sasani is to buy this company at an unrealistic price," chairman Nic Frangos told Reuters in an interview.
"On a competitive bid where there are strategic people buying for strategic reasons, the price tends to get high," he said.
The sale of Interleisure, which holds a 20 percent stake in Sasani, is part of the unbundling of Servgro International which together with Kersaf Ltd jointly own Interleisure.

Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealers said earlier that there was talk that the Interleisure selling price had jumped to around 1.5 billion rand or between nine and 10.50 rand a share -- well above its closing price on Tuesday of eight rand. The price was previously expected to be around 1.2 billion rand.
Frangos said that the deal was "very far down the track" and that a decision was probably imminent.

He added, however, that the Johannesburg stock market had put too much store by the potential deal. Concerns that the Interleisure asking price was too high has knocked over 30 percent off Sasani's share price in the past three weeks, although 10 percent of this was recouped on Tuesday.
"The market has perceived (the deal) as almost a winner takes all situation. But that is not true as Sasani, if it doesn't get the deal, will still be alive and well afterwards," he said.

Frangos said that Sasani in the 15 months to end-June will achieve its forecast earnings per share target of around 3.6 cents. The group, which has changed its year end to June 30, recently reported 12-month results to end-March at 3.4 cents a share.
He said the group's core operations, the Movie Camera Co and Video Lab which it recently bought, were mature, had a history of strong growth rates and were extremely well managed.
Other than the Interleisure deal, Sasani was eyeing a number of other acquisitions, he said, but did not give further details.

Frangos said that talks over the Interleisure sale had dragged on as the deal had taken many forms since it was first mooted. These included Servgro selling out and Kersaf retaining its stake or both firms pulling out. He did not say what the final deal was likely to be.
Another firm believed to be interested in Interleisure is publishing and media firm Primedia Ltd which issued a cautionary notice on June 17 saying it was in unspecified talks.
Acquisitive Primedia recently bought specialist publishing firm Publico Holdings and has snapped up a number of local radio stations privatised by the state broadcaster.
